descripcion: At B1 you make a simple deduction with must be and can't be about the present, based on real evidence you can see or infer. The past forms, like must have been, come later once this basic present form is automatic.

filas: He must be tired because he worked all night.

ejemplos.texto: She must be really tired after that trip.
That can't be true, it doesn't make sense.
He must be at home, his car is outside.

notas: Must be expresses a strong, confident guess based on evidence.
Can't be is the negative form used to rule something out — not mustn't be.
These deductions are about the present situation, not the past.

contraste.es: Spanish uses deber de + infinitive for similar deductions (debe de estar cansada), which transfers well to English must be.
contraste.de: German has the same structure (Sie muss müde sein – She must be tired), so the positive form transfers directly. The negative does not: German speakers often say she mustn't be tired where English uses she can't be tired.
contraste.it: Italian has close equivalents: deve essere stanca (she must be tired) and non può essere stanca (she can't be tired). The Italian future of probability (sarà stanca) is a separate source of error, producing she will be tired.
contraste.fr: French has close equivalents: elle doit être fatiguée (she must be tired) and elle ne peut pas être fatiguée (she can't be tired). The transfer is direct for present-time deduction.
contraste.pt: Portuguese has the same structure: deve estar cansada (she must be tired) and não pode estar cansada (she can't be tired). Portuguese speakers therefore handle present-time deduction with very little interference.

errores: Using mustn't be instead of can't be to rule something out.
Using must for permission instead of deduction.
Making a deduction without any real evidence.
autochequeo: Is can't be used to rule something out, not mustn't be?
Is the deduction based on real evidence?
Have I used both must be and can't be?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on must be and can't be for present deduction. Check that can't be, not mustn't be, is used to rule something out. Do not rewrite the text.
